mvgam_residcor object description

Source: R/mvgam_residcor-class.R
mvgam_residcor-class.Rd

A mvgam_residcor object returned by function residual_cor(). Run methods(class = "mvgam_residcor") to see the available methods.

Value

Objects of this class are structured as a list with the following components:

cor, cor_se, cor_lower, cor_upper

Posterior summaries of the \(p \times p\) correlation matrix: the posterior mean (the median under robust = TRUE), the posterior SD (the MAD under robust = TRUE) and the limits of the credible interval at the probs levels.

cor_ess

\(p \times p\) matrix of per-entry effective sample sizes of the correlation draws, computed on the Fisher-z scale with posterior::ess_basic(). The diagonal is NA, being fixed at 1. A low value marks a correlation the chains sampled poorly, however narrow its interval.

prob_positive, prob_negative, prob_nonzero

\(p \times p\) matrices of Pr(r > 0), Pr(r < 0) and the larger of the two for every off-diagonal entry. Each measures how well the data determine the sign of a correlation.

sig_cor

The correlation matrix with every entry set to zero where prob_nonzero is at most prob_threshold. plot.mvgam_residcor() draws cor. A hard cut would draw a correlation the data leave uncertain the same as one estimated at zero.

cov, cov_se, cov_lower, cov_upper, cov_ess

Posterior summaries of the residual covariance matrix, with per-entry ESS.

mean_abs_offdiag

A list of point, lower and upper summarising the mean absolute off-diagonal correlation. The mean is taken within each draw and then summarised across draws. The interval then describes the overall strength of correlation.

n_series, series_names

Dimensions of the matrix and the series labels.

pattern, hierarchical, group_label

The residual structure that was summarised.

covariance

"stationary" for the covariance of the latent states, or "innovation" for that of one step's shocks, as residual_cor() was asked.

probs, prob_threshold

The credible interval levels and the prob_nonzero threshold of sig_cor.

Passing partial = TRUE to residual_cor() adds the partial correlations, with one field for each correlation field: prec, prec_se, prec_lower, prec_upper, prec_ess, prec_prob_positive, prec_prob_negative, prec_prob_nonzero

and the thresholded sig_prec. Partial correlations are bounded like correlations. They are summarised on the same Fisher-z scale. plot.mvgam_residcor() with type = "precision" requires them.

Details

In a latent factor model the residual covariance between series is \(\Sigma = Z \Omega Z'\), where \(Z\) holds the factor loadings and \(\Omega\) is the covariance of the latent states. A strong residual correlation between two species can reflect a species interaction (facilitation or competition), a missing covariate, or any other association the predictors in formula leave unexplained (Hui 2016).

The partial correlation between two series conditions on every other series (Ovaskainen et al. 2016). It is computed from the inverse of the correlation matrix, with the diagonal set to 1. Two species with a partial correlation near zero can still be correlated. They are then conditionally independent given the other species. Their association runs through those species. A larger partial correlation suggests a more direct association.

References

Francis KC Hui (2016). BORAL - Bayesian ordination and regression analysis of multivariate abundance data in R. Methods in Ecology and Evolution. 7, 744-750.

Otso Ovaskainen et al. (2016). Using latent variable models to identify large networks of species-to-species associations at different spatial scales. Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 7, 549-555.
